title: First Game in Godot
author: Wheelydope
selftext:
Apologies for the repost, I suck at Reddit. 

This is my first attempt at a game and I’m having a blast making it! After 6 weeks, I have a playable demo with plenty of bugs and fun. I’ve learned a ton so far and never thought I’d be able to do something like this. 

This game is aimed to be an adventure/park sim where you play as the caretaker in a small residential park in the Colorado mountains. The goal is to take care of the land, maintain the ecosystem, build relationships with the residents, learn about the origin of the park, and explore the surrounding areas. 

I’ve been working in Godot 4.7 with Blender, MeshyAI, Codex, Synty assets, and Suno. 

Let me know what you think!

replies.author: TriggerHydrant
replies.body: Yeah same! Just started dipping into assets but it's a different beast

replies.author: Wheelydope
replies.body:
Yeah of course! So I started with generating photos of a character model in ChatGPT. Once I had one I liked, I used a combo of GPT and Nanobanana in Meshy to stylize every other asset based on the character image. Of course I used a ton of placeholders in the beginning too. 

Meshy has a lot of built in animations too, but not everything I wanted. I actually had Codex build some animations for the deer, fishing, etc by giving it reference videos of real life scenarios. It was terrible at it, but it gave me something basic to manually tweak in Blender. 

Tbh, this all experimental and I have no idea what I’m doing.
